sources.citation: game-design: an adjustable torque screwdriver drives a screw and slips at its setting, so it has drive and torque, with no conductor size limit. The torque a terminal needs comes from the device's own marking (NFPA 70-2023 Art. 110.14(D), cited by number), never from a torque table.

ISO 6789-1:2017 (cited by number) classes an adjustable, graduated torque screwdriver as a setting tool, Type II Class D, with a maximum permissible deviation of plus or minus 6 % over its specified range, from its lowest marked value to its maximum. Several makers' adjustable torque screwdrivers of the 1-5 N·m class state plus or minus 6 % to ISO 6789 (typical published figures, paraphrased, not one vendor's).
game-design: its 1/4 in hex bit holder (hex-shank bits, ISO 1173 cited by number) takes slotted, cross-recess (Phillips and Pozidriv) and square bits, all assumed in the kit; bit sizes are names.
